question: Press reports indicate that, prompted by the exhaustion of their storage capacity and the critical state of the plastic recycling industry, Italy’s sorting facilities have, since 12 November 2025, either refused to accept any more plastic packaging waste or reduced their intake, leading many councils throughout Sicily to limit plastic waste collection.

In addition, storage facilities are forced to stockpile these materials, a major fire risk. Far from being an isolated case, this issue concerns the country as a whole, as the insufficient number and uneven distribution of sorting centres in southern Italy has compelled councils there to pay to ship their waste to other regions.

This state of affairs could compromise the objectives set out by Directives 2008/98/EC, 94/62/EC and 2019/904/EU regarding waste, packaging and single-use plastics respectively and jeopardise the Union's extended producer responsibility (EPR) policies.

While Italy has postponed the introduction of the plastic tax to 31 December 2026, the country’s competition authority has highlighted that public funds are, at best, only covering 20 % of municipal plastic packaging waste collection costs, four times less than what was promised. In the light of the above: 1.
Is the Commission aware of this situation, and has it discussed it with the competent Italian authorities?
What steps will it take to ensure that Italy can continue to collect and recycle plastic waste?

How will the Commission ensure that Italy complies with its EPR obligations and reimburses at least 80 % of municipal plastic packaging waste collection costs without increasing the national waste tax (TARI)?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.3.2026) The Commission, in response to the challenges in the plastics recycling sector, adopted in December 2025 a package of measures to accelerate Europe's transition to a circular economy1. Moreover, rules for recycled content in beverage bottles under the Single-Use Plastics Directive2 were voted on 6 February 20263 in favour by Member States.

This could help strengthen the sector’s competitiveness. EU law mandates Member States to establish extended producer responsibility scheme for packaging, in line with the polluter pays principle, and also to set up separate collection of packaging waste4. This will help Member States achieve the recycling targets for packaging waste and eventually facilitate high-quality recycling5.

The 2023 Early Warning Report for Italy highlighted that the recycling rate of plastic packaging waste was 6.2 percentage points below the 2020 EU target of 50%6, whereas recommended to continue pursue policies that maintain and improve performance levels on collection and recycling of packaging waste. The Commission is working with national authorities to support implementation of EU law.

It also monitors compliance with the Waste Framework Directive, Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation, and Single-Use Plastics Directive and may, where necessary, use its powers under the Treaties.

economy-boosting-circularity-plastics_en. 2 Directive (EU) 2019/904 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 5 June 2019 on the reduction of the impact of certain plastic products on the environment, OJ L 155, 12.6.2019, p. 1–19.

3 Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/2683 of 30 November 2023 laying down rules for the application of Directive (EU) 2019/904 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the calculation, verification and reporting of data on recycled plastic content in single-use plastic beverage bottles, OJ L, 2023/2683, 1.12.2023.

4 Directive (EU) 2025/1892 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 September 2025 amending Directive 2008/98/EC on waste, OJ L, 2025/1892, 26.9.2025. 5 Regulation (EU) 2025/40 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 December 2024 on packaging and packaging waste, amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and Directive (EU) 2019/904, and repealing Directive 94/62/EC, OJ L, 2025/40, 22.1.2025.
